title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Helsinki’s Kallio Streets
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra “meet in the middle” to find the fastest route across a street-map graph. The visualization shows how two simultaneous shortest-path searches reduce explored areas while still guaranteeing optimal paths.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ Helsinki (Kallio) street graph in motion with **Bidirectional Dijkstra**!

In this visualization, we run Dijkstra from the **start** and from the **goal** at the same time. Each search expands frontier nodes based on current best-known distances, and the algorithm stops when the two frontiers meet with the smallest combined cost—still guaranteeing the **optimal shortest path** on weighted graphs. 🧠📍

Because real streets form a weighted graph (edges = roads, weights = travel cost like time/distance), bidirectional search effectively cuts down the explored space compared to a single-source Dijkstra—especially on large road networks. 🌐🔎

fb_caption:
In Helsinki (Kallio), we visualize **graph search** using **Bidirectional Dijkstra**—two shortest-path searches expand from start and goal simultaneously until they meet. This approach explores less of the street-map graph than classic single-direction Dijkstra, while still guaranteeing the optimal route. 🙌
